correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the incidence graph of 2- and 3-subsets of [5] directly (20 vertices, degree 3, 30 edges). For a removed k-set S leaving c tree components, edge counting proves 2k=10+e(S)+c, hence k≥6 and at k=6 only (e(S),c)=(0,2) or (1,1). Wrote a separate union-find forest/cycle enumerator over all C(20,6)=38,760 choices, obtaining exactly 2,860, with counts 760/2100 and forest profiles (1,13):360,(2,12):180,(3,11):120,(4,10):20,(7,7):80,(14):2100. Generated all 120 symbol permutations times subset-complementation (240 distinct automorphisms), proved they preserve adjacency and cover 2,860 sets in 19 orbits with claimed sizes. Conversely side-preserving aut induces an automorphism of T(5), whose five maximum stars force S5, so Aut(D) has no further elements. Full finite enumeration is exhaustive at this graph order, not a bound extrapolated to other graphs.

value.rationale: A complete and reproducible natural finite graph invariant: not merely the already known scalar decycling number, but all minimizers, induced residual forest shapes and automorphism orbits. Exact orbit decomposition is independently useful for combinatorial optimization and symmetry reductions; complete finite classification is a legitimate substantive result.

final_claim: For the 20-vertex Desargues graph D≅GP(10,3)≅H(5,2), its feedback vertex number is the known value six, and exactly 2,860 six-vertex sets are optimal: 760 span no deleted edge and leave two forest components, 2,100 span one edge and leave a fourteen-vertex tree. There are 19 Aut(D)-orbits under the full 240-element group, with orbit sizes 20×2,60×3,120×6,240×8 and the six claimed forest-component order profiles.
limitations: Only Desargues graph (20 vertices) is classified, and known optimum cardinality is prior.
